articles.title: Electricity prices: Three reasons why they are high in the UK
articles.summary: Ofgem has announced a 26% rise in the energy price cap - here's why Britons pay more for power than many other European nations.
articles.body:
Bills are set to rise for millions of households, after Ofgem announced that the energy price cap will rise by 26% in January.

The main reason for the increase is international gas prices, Ofgem says, but UK energy prices - particularly for electricity - have been high for some time.

1. The cost of wholesale gas often sets the electricity price

The price energy suppliers pay for electricity is often determined by a bidding process, with each generating company saying what it would be willing to accept to produce one unit of electricity.

Once built, the cost of generating power from renewables like wind and solar is relatively low, so these typically come in with the cheapest bid. Nuclear might come next.

Gas generators often have high costs because they have to buy fuel to generate electricity as well as paying a "carbon price" - a charge for emissions.

The wholesale market price is set by the most expensive unit of electricity needed to meet demand.

This means that even if gas only generates a small proportion of electricity at a given time it can set the overall market price.

So when gas costs spike - as has happened following the wars in Ukraine and Iran - electricity prices do too.

Not all electricity generation is directly priced in this way. For example, newer wind and solar farms are typically guaranteed a fixed price, irrespective of the wholesale price, while some generators enter into direct contracts with suppliers.

In the first quarter of 2027, the contribution of wholesale energy costs to a typical annual household bill in Great Britain will be £1,216 - up from £604 in the first quarter of 2026 and up from £373 in the winter of 2019-20. These figures account for both electricity and gas.

Northern Ireland operates on a separate system to the rest of the UK, being part of the Single Electricity Market with the Republic of Ireland.

2. Other countries have a different energy mix

Analysts say that one of the reasons why energy prices are relatively high in the UK is because of the country's reliance on natural gas - leaving households exposed to gas price spikes.

While renewables are generating more electricity than a decade ago, a relatively high share still comes from natural gas.

In 2025 31% of the UK's electricity was produced in that way.

This compares with just 3% in France, which generated the majority of its electricity - 69% - from nuclear power.

The US has a higher share of natural gas in its electricity generation mix than the UK - 40% - but American wholesale gas prices are considerably lower thanks to the shale gas production boom of the past 20 years.

Most UK homes also rely on gas for heating, for example, so are directly hit when gas prices rise - as well as those who use electricity.

3. The UK is building much more electricity grid infrastructure

Another reason energy bills have risen in recent years is down to the cost of expanding and modernising the UK's energy networks.

Those investments are partly to upgrade an ageing gas grid but also to accommodate new wind and solar farms and transmit their power to homes and businesses.

The network costs contribution to a typical annual energy bill will be £417 in the first quarter of 2027, an increase of £197 from £220 in the winter of 2019-20.

"We've probably underinvested in the last decade and now we're trying to catch up so there's quite a lot of spending," says Frankie Mayo, an energy analyst from Ember Energy.

There are other costs associated with renewable electricity. Many older projects are paid a subsidy on top of the wholesale electricity price, which was designed to encourage investment at a time when renewables were particularly expensive.

Many of these projects are still under contract and so still receive the subsidy, although the government has moved much of these costs off bills and onto general taxation.

However the government and some energy groups argue that reducing our national reliance on volatile international gas prices via the government's clean power push will keep down the UK's wholesale electricity costs and mean household bills will be lower than they would otherwise have been.

This would be by reducing the amount of time in each year that gas sets the wholesale electricity price.

A great deal though depends on future wholesale gas prices which are impossible to accurately forecast.

Some analysts, including the government's Climate Change Committee, also say the government should go further to remove policy costs from household electricity bills and meet them through general taxation instead.

That would encourage people to use cleaner electricity rather than gas to heat their homes, they argue.

"The way you allocate those costs matters," says Mayo.

"They may be being put on bills or they may be being paid by consumers in other ways that are less visible, such as taxes."

articles.title: Kilmar Abrego Garcia, who fought his mistaken deportation, leaves the US voluntarily for Spain
articles.summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — Kilmar Abrego Garcia, a Salvadoran national who fought his mistaken deportation, left the U. voluntarily for Spain on Tuesday, officials an...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON (AP) — Kilmar Abrego Garcia , a Salvadoran national who fought his mistaken deportation , left the U.S. voluntarily for Spain on Tuesday, officials and his attorneys said, in what could bring an end to a defining saga of the Trump administration's immigration crackdown.

Abrego Garcia was arrested in Baltimore in March 2025 and deported to a Salvadoran prison in what an official later called an "administrative error." His departure to Spain comes after months of legal wrangling as he battled the administration's drive to deport him to Africa.

Abrego Garcia, his lawyers and the Trump administration sought to portray the departure as a victory.

"I am leaving happy. I am leaving with my freedom," Abrego Garcia said in a statement. "I am leaving with the love of an entire community, with people who cared for me, believed in me, and joined my family in this fight."

The Department of Homeland Security said Tuesday night that he self-deported to Spain as part of a removal order and that he didn't receive any incentives and won't be allowed back in to the U.S. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said in a post on X that he was "delighted" about Abrego Garcia's departure, listing off a familiar litany of allegations for why he should be deported, including that he was a gang member, an accusation Abrego Garcia has repeatedly denied.

But Simon Sandoval-Moshenberg, an attorney for Abrego Garcia, called this a temporary departure as he "waits out the end of this administration." He said Abrego Garcia has many options to return to U.S.

"We don't expect that to happen under this administration, which we know will never give him a fair shake, but we expect that the next administration will prioritize reunifying this family and bringing him back to Maryland," he said.

A judge told Abrego Garcia to self-deport by Tuesday, according to a person familiar with the matter, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to publicly discuss the case.

Video posted by ABC News showed Abrego Garcia walking through Washington Dulles International Airport with his wife and others, including an official from We Are CASA, an advocacy group that has supported Abrego Garcia and his family.

Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen, who met with Abrego Garcia while he was pressing for his release from a Salvadoran mega-prison, described Abrego Garcia as a "free man" and said he is traveling to a country of his choice.

"I am relieved that he will be safe, in a country of his choosing, and free — including from this Administration's constant persecution," he said in a statement.

Abrego Garcia's deportation in early 2025 came as the Trump administration was ramping up its immigration crackdown, promising to deport 1 million people annually. Through an infusion of billions of dollars approved by Congress, the administration later supercharged its immigration enforcement capabilities, growing its cadre of immigration officers, expanding detention capabilities and pushing to deport an increasing number of people.

He was fighting against a second deportation to a series of African countries proposed by DHS officials.

Abrego Garcia was mistakenly deported in March 2025

The 31-year-old Abrego Garcia has an American wife and child and has lived in Maryland for years, but he immigrated to the U.S. illegally as a teenager. In 2019, an immigration judge ruled that he could not be deported to El Salvador because he faced danger there from a gang that had threatened his family. The judge allowed him to live and work in the U.S. under Immigration and Customs Enforcement supervision, but he was not given residency status.

His deportation in 2025 involved being sent to a mega-prison in El Salvador known as CECOT, which activists say is rife with abuses and where inmates are packed into cells and never allowed outside.

Facing public pressure and a court order , President Donald Trump's administration brought him back in June 2025, but only after securing an indictment charging him with human smuggling in Tennessee.

A federal judge dismissed that case in May, finding that the Justice Department's pursuit of criminal charges was designed to punish Abrego Garcia for challenging his deportation. The government is appealing.

The Trump administration vowed to deport him to a third country, threatening to send him to Uganda, Eswatini, Ghana, and, most recently, Liberia .

Abrego Garcia fought his deportation in court

Abrego Garcia had argued that if he were going to be deported, it should be to Costa Rica, which previously agreed to take him. But Todd Lyons, the former acting director of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, said in a March 2026 memo that deporting Abrego Garcia to Costa Rica would be "prejudicial to the United States."

Lyons wrote that Abrego Garcia should be sent to Liberia because the U.S. has spent governmental resources and political capital in negotiating for it to accept third-country nationals. The push for deportation to Liberia continued even after the U.S. signed an agreement with Costa Rica to accept deportees who cannot legally be returned to their home countries.

His case took an unusual turn on Oct. 6, 2026, when, five minutes before a hearing expected to determine whether U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement could detain and deport Ábrego Garcia to the West African country of Liberia, attorneys for both sides left the courtroom, along with Abrego Garcia.

When they returned 15 minutes later, it was announced the hearing was canceled. The two sides then gathered for another 90 minutes before leaving the courthouse without explanation. Abrego Garcia's attorney said only the court case was not ready to proceed and he instructed reporters to watch the docket to learn the status of the case.

Associated Press reporter Rebecca Santana contributed.
authors: ALANNA DURKIN RICHER, HALLIE GOLDEN and MICHAEL KUNZELMAN

articles.title: Imigrante deportado por engano deixa os EUA voluntariamente  | G1
articles.standfirst: Kilmar Abrego Garcia foi enviado a El Salvador em 2025 por um erro administrativo e, desde então, enfrentava uma batalha judicial contra novas tentativas de deportação.
articles.summary: Kilmar Abrego Garcia foi enviado a El Salvador em 2025 por um erro administrativo e, desde então, enfrentava uma batalha judicial contra novas tentativas de deportação.
articles.body:
Kilmar Abrego, o imigrante cuja deportação indevida para El Salvador o tornou um símbolo das políticas imigratórias agressivas do presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, comparece para uma apresentação no escritório local do ICE em Baltimore, três dias após sua liberação da custódia criminal no Tennessee — em Baltimore, Maryland, EUA, 25 de agosto de 2025. — Foto: REUTERS/Elizabeth Frantz

Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Kilmar Abrego García, imigrante salvadorenho que foi deportado por engano dos Estados Unidos em 2025, deixou o país voluntariamente na terça-feira (24) e viajou para a Espanha , segundo autoridades e advogados.

A saída ocorre após meses de disputas judiciais contra a tentativa do governo Donald Trump de deportá-lo para países africanos. O salvadorenho chegou a Madri nesta manhã.

A mudança de García pode encerrar um dos casos mais emblemáticos da política migratória do governo Trump, segundo o veículo de notícia americano Associated Press (AP).

Abrego Garcia foi preso em Baltimore, em março de 2025, e enviado a uma prisão em El Salvador . O episódio foi posteriormente reconhecido por um funcionário do governo americano como um “erro administrativo”. Desde então, ele enfrentou uma série de disputas judiciais para evitar novas deportações.

“Estou saindo feliz. Estou saindo com minha liberdade”, afirmou Abrego Garcia em comunicado. Ele também agradeceu às pessoas que apoiaram sua família durante a batalha judicial.

O Departamento de Segurança Interna dos Estados Unidos (DHS, na sigla em inglês) afirmou que ele se autodeportou para a Espanha como parte de uma ordem de remoção, que não recebeu incentivos para deixar o país e que não poderá retornar aos Estados Unidos.

O secretário de Segurança Interna, Markwayne Mullin, comemorou a saída em uma publicação nas redes sociais e voltou a mencionar acusações de que Abrego Garcia teria ligação com uma gangue. Ele nega as acusações.

Já o advogado Simon Sandoval-Moshenberg afirmou que a viagem é temporária e que o imigrante pretende aguardar o fim do atual governo americano. Segundo o advogado, há possibilidades de que ele retorne aos Estados Unidos no futuro.

“Não esperamos que isso aconteça durante esta administração, que sabemos que nunca lhe dará uma oportunidade justa, mas esperamos que a próxima administração priorize a reunificação desta família e o traga de volta a Maryland”, afirmou.

Kilmar Abrego Garcia e sua esposa, Jennifer Vasquez Sura, deixam o Tribunal Distrital dos EUA no dia de uma audiência em seu caso, em Greenbelt, Maryland, EUA, 6 de outubro de 2026 — Foto: REUTERS/Nathan Howard/Arquivo

Deportação por engano e disputa judicial

Abrego Garcia, de 31 anos, viveu durante anos em Maryland, nos Estados Unidos, e tem esposa e filho americanos. Ele imigrou ilegalmente para o país ainda adolescente.

Em 2019, um juiz de imigração determinou que ele não poderia ser deportado para El Salvador porque havia risco de perseguição por uma gangue que ameaçava sua família. A decisão permitiu que ele permanecesse nos Estados Unidos e trabalhasse sob supervisão do Serviço de Imigração e Alfândega (ICE), mas sem receber status de residente.

Apesar da decisão, ele foi deportado em março de 2025 para El Salvador e enviado ao Centro de Confinamento do Terrorismo (CECOT), um megapresídio que tem sido alvo de denúncias de abusos.

Em julho de 2025, conforme noticiado pelo g1 com informações da AP, Abrego Garcia relatou em documentos judiciais que havia sofrido agressões físicas, privação de sono e tortura psicológica durante o período em que esteve preso. Ele afirmou ter sido chutado e espancado, obrigado a permanecer ajoelhado durante a noite e ameaçado por agentes penitenciários.

As alegações foram apresentadas por Abrego Garcia em documentos judiciais.

Pressionado pela opinião pública e por uma ordem judicial, o governo Trump o trouxe de volta aos Estados Unidos em junho de 2025, mas após obter uma acusação criminal contra ele por suspeita de tráfico de pessoas no Tennessee.

Em maio, um juiz federal rejeitou o caso, entendendo que a tentativa do Departamento de Justiça de processá-lo tinha como objetivo puni-lo por contestar a deportação. O governo recorreu da decisão.

Governo tentou deportá-lo para países africanos

Após o retorno de Abrego Garcia aos Estados Unidos, o governo Trump voltou a defender a deportação do imigrante para um terceiro país. Entre os destinos cogitados estavam Uganda, Eswatini, Gana e, mais recentemente, Libéria.

Abrego Garcia argumentou que, caso fosse deportado, deveria ser enviado à Costa Rica, país que havia concordado em recebê-lo. Em um memorando de março de 2026, porém, um ex-diretor interino do ICE afirmou que a deportação para a Costa Rica seria prejudicial aos interesses dos Estados Unidos.

Kilmar Abrego Garcia, deportado por engano para prisão em El Salvador — Foto: Murray Osorio PLLC vía AP

A tentativa de enviá-lo à Libéria continuou mesmo depois de os Estados Unidos firmarem um acordo com a Costa Rica para receber deportados que não pudessem ser enviados legalmente aos países de origem.

Em 6 de outubro de 2026, o caso teve uma reviravolta. Pouco antes de uma audiência que deveria decidir se o ICE poderia detê-lo e deportá-lo para a Libéria, advogados dos dois lados deixaram o tribunal junto com Abrego Garcia.

Quando retornaram, cerca de 15 minutos depois, a audiência foi cancelada. As partes ainda se reuniram por aproximadamente 90 minutos, mas deixaram o tribunal sem explicar o que havia ocorrido.

A saída de Abrego Garcia para a Espanha acontece após esse impasse judicial e em meio à disputa sobre o destino do imigrante.

articles.title: Frente fria deve provocar chuva forte em SP e no Rio; veja previsão | G1
articles.standfirst: Chuva deve ganhar força em São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro e Minas Gerais a partir desta quarta-feira (25). Sul e Centro-Oeste também terão temporais, enquanto calor e tempo seco predominam no Nordeste.
articles.summary: Chuva pode chegar a 200 mm no litoral paulista e a 150 mm na Região Serrana do Rio. Sul e Centro-Oeste terão temporais; Nordeste terá calor e tempo seco.
articles.body:
Segundo a Climatempo, o avanço do sistema deve intensificar as instabilidades principalmente entre esta quarta (25) e quinta-feira (26). — Foto: Vanessa Rodrigues/Jornal A Tribuna

Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Uma nova frente fria deve avançar pela costa do Sudeste nesta quarta-feira (25). A passagem do sistema deve favorecer chuvas fortes e volumosas em áreas de São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro e Minas Gerais.

A previsão indica que os acumulados podem chegar a 200 milímetros em dois dias no litoral paulista, o que pode provocar alagamentos, enxurradas e deslizamentos de terra.

Segundo a Climatempo, o avanço do sistema deve intensificar as instabilidades principalmente entre esta quarta e quinta-feira (26).

O maior volume de chuva é esperado no litoral de São Paulo, mas a Grande São Paulo, o Vale do Paraíba e o Vale do Ribeira também devem registrar pancadas fortes e persistentes.

A previsão aponta acumulados de até 150 milímetros na Região Serrana do Rio de Janeiro e 120 milímetros no leste de Minas Gerais entre quarta e quinta-feira.

No Sul, a chuva deve continuar em áreas do Paraná, Santa Catarina e norte do Rio Grande do Sul.

O Centro-Oeste também deve registrar novas pancadas, principalmente em Mato Grosso do Sul, Mato Grosso, Goiás e no Distrito Federal.

Já no Nordeste, o tempo seco e o calor intenso devem predominar em boa parte da região, embora áreas do oeste da Bahia possam ter chuva forte.

Frente fria deve intensificar chuva em São Paulo

Esta quarta deve começar com chuva em áreas da metade norte de São Paulo, mas as instabilidades tendem a aumentar ao longo do dia, principalmente durante a tarde e a noite.

As áreas com maior previsão de chuva incluem a Grande São Paulo, o Vale do Ribeira, o Vale do Paraíba, a Baixada Santista, o Litoral Norte e regiões próximas à Serra do Mar.

No litoral, os acumulados podem superar 100 milímetros somente na quarta-feira, principalmente entre a Baixada Santista e o Litoral Norte, segundo a Climatempo.

No Rio de Janeiro, a frente fria deve intensificar as pancadas de chuva a partir de quarta-feira, principalmente durante a tarde e a noite.

A previsão indica chuva forte em diferentes áreas do estado, inclusive na capital, na Região Serrana e em municípios próximos à divisa com São Paulo.

Em Minas Gerais, as instabilidades devem atingir principalmente o Triângulo Mineiro e as regiões oeste, centro-sul e leste do estado, incluindo a Grande Belo Horizonte.

No leste mineiro, a previsão aponta acumulados de até 120 milímetros em dois dias.

O Espírito Santo também deve registrar pancadas de chuva, principalmente nas áreas do sul e do interior.

Apesar das instabilidades, o calor deve continuar predominando em boa parte do Sudeste durante a quarta-feira.

Uma queda das temperaturas deve ficar mais evidente na quinta (26), com a entrada de ventos mais frios associados à passagem da frente fria.

Em São Paulo (SP), por exemplo, a máxima pode cair para 20°C na quinta-feira, segundo o Inmet . No Rio de Janeiro (RJ), a previsão é de máxima de 28°C.

Mapa mostra previsão de chuva para esta quinta (25/11) em todo o Brasil. — Foto: CPTEC/Inpe

No Sul, as pancadas de chuva devem continuar nesta quarta-feira (25), principalmente no norte do Rio Grande do Sul, em Santa Catarina e no Paraná.

As instabilidades devem ganhar força durante a tarde, quando há possibilidade de temporais isolados. No oeste paranaense e catarinense, os volumes de chuva podem ser elevados.

A partir de quinta-feira, a chegada de uma massa de ar frio deve derrubar as temperaturas.

As mínimas podem ficar abaixo de 10°C nas serras gaúcha e catarinense.

Em Curitiba (PR), a previsão é de mínima de 13°C e máxima de 18°C. Não há, porém, indicação de frio persistente nem de formação de geadas.

No Centro-Oeste, a combinação de calor e umidade deve favorecer pancadas de chuva de moderada a forte intensidade nesta quarta-feira (25), principalmente em Mato Grosso do Sul, no sudoeste de Mato Grosso, no leste de Goiás e no Distrito Federal.

Em Mato Grosso do Sul, a chuva pode começar pela manhã, sobretudo nas áreas próximas à fronteira com o Paraguai. Nas demais localidades, as pancadas devem se concentrar entre a tarde e a noite.

Na quinta-feira, as instabilidades devem persistir em grande parte da região. Apesar da chuva, o calor deve continuar predominando.

Temperaturas mínimas previstas para esta quarta (25/11) em todo o Brasil. — Foto: CPTEC/Inpe

Norte e Nordeste terão calor e pancadas de chuva

No Nordeste, o sol e as temperaturas elevadas devem predominar nesta quarta-feira (25), principalmente no Sertão e no Meio-Norte.

A umidade relativa do ar pode ficar entre 20% e 30% em áreas do interior.

As chuvas devem se concentrar no oeste da Bahia, onde há possibilidade de pancadas fortes. No litoral, podem ocorrer chuvas fracas e passageiras. Em Teresina (PI), a máxima pode chegar a 41°C.

No Norte, há previsão de pancadas de moderada a forte intensidade no Acre, em Rondônia, no centro-sul do Amazonas e do Pará, em Tocantins e no norte do Amapá.

Na quinta-feira, as chuvas devem persistir principalmente no Amazonas e em Rondônia, além de áreas da Bahia, do Maranhão e do Piauí. O calor deve continuar nas duas regiões.

articles.title: Temporal alaga casas, comércios e escolas em Brazópolis | G1
articles.standfirst: Em Poços de Caldas, a água invadiu ruas do centro da cidade e atrapalhou o trânsito. Cristina também foi atingida pelas chuvas e deve declarar situação de emergência.
articles.summary: Em Poços de Caldas, a água invadiu ruas do centro da cidade e atrapalhou o trânsito. Cristina também foi atingida pelas chuvas e deve declarar situação de emergência.
articles.body:
Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

O temporal que atingiu o Sul de Minas na noite de terça-feira (24) causou alagamentos em Brazópolis , Cristina e Poços de Caldas .

Em Brazópolis, a chuva começou por volta das 23h e seguiu pela madrugada. Boa parte da cidade ficou sob a água. O local mais atingido foi o distrito de Cruz Vera, segundo a Defesa Civil. Várias residências foram tomadas pela água.

Houve alagamento também na região central, onde a antiga estação, várias casas e estabelecimentos comerciais foram invadidos pela enxurrada.

Duas escolas municipais e uma estadual ficaram algadas e tiveram as aulas suspensas.

Chuva alaga Brazópolis e água invade casas, comércios e escolas — Foto: Redes sociais

De acordo com a Defesa Civil, há moradores desabrigados e desalojados. Não há registro de feridos. O órgão está fazendo o levantamento dos danos na manhã desta quarta-feira (25). Equipe da Defesa Civil estadual deve ir até a região para avaliar os estragos.

A rodovia MG-295, que liga Brazópolis a Paraisópolis, ficou alagada e segue interditada. O rio da Vergem Grande transbordou e a água está passando por cima da ponte.

A chuva também causou transtornos em Poços de Caldas e Cristina.

Em Cristina, choveu 100 milímetros entre as 22h de terça e 3h desta quarta-feira. A cidade deve declarar situação de emergência.

Em Poços de Caldas, a água tomou algumas das ruas mais importantes da região central, como a Junqueiras, Rio Grande do Norte e Nico Duarte, atrapalhando o trânsito. Não há registro de desabrigados ou feridos.

Os pedidos constantes dos fãs por um novo reencontro e a oportunidade de criar uma residência artística inédita estiveram entre os fatores que levaram Sandy e Junior a voltar aos palcos em 2027 . "A galera parece que nunca se acostumou direito com o fim da dupla Sandy e Júnior" , avaliou a cantora.

Durante a coletiva de lançamento do projeto "Nada É Por Acaso", nesta terça-feira (24), os irmãos afirmaram que as manifestações do público continuaram mesmo após a turnê de 2019 e que o formato da residência abriu espaço para uma experiência diferente de tudo o que já haviam feito na carreira.

🔍 Residência artística é uma temporada de apresentações em que um artista ou banda concentra vários shows no mesmo palco por um período determinado. É uma opção às tradicionais turnês que percorrem várias cidades.

Segundo Sandy, os questionamentos sobre uma nova volta continuaram ao longo dos anos, mesmo depois do reencontro para a turnê comemorativa de 2019: "As pessoas continuam falando: 'Quando vai ter de novo?'."

A cantora afirmou que a ideia de um novo projeto começou a ganhar força quando diferentes fatores passaram a coincidir, incluindo a disponibilidade dos artistas, do estádio e dos organizadores.

Além da resposta dos fãs, a proposta de uma residência artística ajudou a diferenciar o novo projeto do reencontro realizado há oito anos. Segundo Junior, a intenção era evitar repetir a mesma fórmula da turnê anterior.

"Não dá para voltar e fazer mais do mesmo. A gente já fez aquela turnê, já teve aquele reencontro", disse.

O cantor explicou que permanecer durante um mês no mesmo local amplia as possibilidades de criação e permite desenvolver experiências que não seriam viáveis em uma turnê tradicional.

"Quando você tira isso da frente, você não tem bloqueio criativo. Você pode fazer um palco do jeito que você quiser, você pode fazer instalação, você pode vestir o estádio com o que você quiser, trabalhar na experiência", avaliou.

A residência artística "Nada É Por Acaso" terá seis apresentações no Nubank Parque, em São Paulo (SP), nos dias 1º, 3, 9, 11, 23 e 25 de julho de 2027. Será a primeira vez que a dupla fará uma temporada de shows desse tipo em um estádio.

Durante a coletiva, os artistas adiantaram que o espetáculo terá estrutura maior que a da turnê "Nossa História", com balé, banda e experiências espalhadas pelo estádio. O repertório deve revisitar várias fases da carreira e incluir músicas menos conhecidas.

Para a equipe do projeto, a residência também busca destacar a relação construída entre os irmãos e o público ao longo de décadas.

O diretor-geral Raoni Carneiro afirmou que essa conexão foi um dos pontos centrais na concepção do espetáculo: "Não é mais só sobre Sandy e Júnior. É sobre Sandy, Júnior e o público."

articles.summary: Pyongyang deu 48 horas para o representante deixar o país; escritório havia sido reaberto em outubro.
articles.body:
Ministro das Relações Exteriores da Suíça, Ignazio Cassis, se reúne com a chanceler norte-coreana, Choe Son Hui, em Pyongyang, em 30 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: Korean Central News Agency/Korea News Service via AP

A Coreia do Norte exigiu nesta quarta-feira (25) o fechamento do novo escritório diplomático da Suíça em Pyongyang e ordenou que o principal diplomata responsável pela representação deixe o país em até 48 horas.

Um dia antes, Kim Yo Jong, irmã do líder norte-coreano Kim Jong Un e uma figura influente do regime, ameaçou fechar o escritório e condenou a Suíça por impor sanções a um acampamento juvenil no leste da Coreia do Norte por seu suposto papel na transferência de crianças de áreas da Ucrânia ocupadas pela Rússia.

A Agência Central de Notícias da Coreia (KCNA) informou que um alto funcionário do Ministério das Relações Exteriores convocou Astier Sylvain, chefe do escritório diplomático suíço aberto em Pyongyang no mês passado, e entregou a ele uma notificação exigindo o fechamento da representação e sua saída do país, em protesto contra as sanções suíças ao Acampamento Internacional Infantil Songdowon, em Wonsan. Segundo a agência, o ministério declarou Sylvain persona non grata.

Kim Yo Jong, uma das principais autoridades de política externa de Pyongyang, classificou as sanções suíças como um “ato abertamente hostil” e uma violação da soberania da Coreia do Norte em um comunicado divulgado na terça-feira. Ela afirmou que o Acampamento Internacional Infantil Songdowon, localizado na cidade costeira de Wonsan, apoiava uma cooperação “legítima” entre Coreia do Norte e Rússia, mas não abordou diretamente as acusações ocidentais de que algumas crianças ucranianas sequestradas pelas forças russas teriam sido enviadas ao local para serem reeducadas.

A Coreia do Norte estreitou significativamente seus laços com a Rússia durante a guerra na Ucrânia, enviando milhares de soldados e grandes carregamentos de armas nos últimos anos para apoiar a invasão em larga escala promovida pelo presidente russo Vladimir Putin, possivelmente em troca de ajuda e transferência de tecnologia militar. O fortalecimento dos laços com Moscou e Pequim tem sido um dos principais fatores por trás da política externa cada vez mais assertiva de Kim Jong Un, que busca tirar ainda mais a Coreia do Norte do isolamento e posicionar o país como parte de uma frente unida contra Washington.

O ministro das Relações Exteriores da Suíça, Ignazio Cassis, viajou à Coreia do Norte no fim de outubro, quando o país europeu abriu um escritório diplomático em Pyongyang. Na ocasião, ele manteve conversas com altas autoridades norte-coreanas, incluindo a ministra das Relações Exteriores, Choe Son Hui, sobre a “promoção do diálogo e da cooperação”, informou a KCNA.

Ao incluir o acampamento Songdowon, no início deste mês, em seu conjunto mais amplo de sanções relacionadas à invasão da Ucrânia pela Rússia, as autoridades suíças afirmaram que o local participa de programas que envolvem a transferência de crianças ucranianas de territórios ocupados pela Rússia para a Coreia do Norte e as expõe a propaganda e atividades destinadas a promover narrativas pró-Rússia.

O Reino Unido, em maio, e a União Europeia, em setembro, impuseram sanções semelhantes ao acampamento Songdowon, congelando seus ativos e proibindo transações financeiras com a instituição. O impacto prático dessas medidas, no entanto, não está claro, considerando os limitados vínculos financeiros da Coreia do Norte com países europeus.

A Suíça estabeleceu relações diplomáticas com a Coreia do Norte em 1974 e é um dos poucos países ocidentais que mantêm diálogo com o país.

A Agência Suíça para o Desenvolvimento e a Cooperação abriu um “escritório de cooperação” em Pyongyang em 1997, voltado principalmente para programas humanitários, mas a representação foi fechada em março de 2020, quando a Coreia do Norte fechou suas fronteiras durante a pandemia de Covid-19.

O governo suíço havia afirmado que o novo escritório diplomático em Pyongyang, subordinado à Embaixada da Suíça em Pequim, ajudaria a fortalecer os contatos diretos com autoridades norte-coreanas e a promover o diálogo.

O Departamento Federal de Relações Exteriores da Suíça afirmou na terça-feira que o país pretendia “manter canais de diálogo” apesar das divergências com outros governos. “A reabertura do escritório é independente da nossa política de sanções, seja em relação às sanções da ONU relacionadas ao programa nuclear da Coreia do Norte ou às sanções da União Europeia adotadas pela Suíça no contexto da guerra da Rússia contra a Ucrânia”, afirmou o órgão em comunicado à Associated Press.

articles.title: Novo sítio rupestre no Piauí tem gravuras ameaçadas por pichações | G1
articles.standfirst: Área de aproximadamente 1 hectare reúne desenhos de lagartos, figuras humanas e símbolos misteriosos em grandes rochas no Parque Estadual Cânion do Rio Poti.
articles.summary: Área de aproximadamente 1 hectare reúne desenhos de lagartos, figuras humanas e símbolos misteriosos em grandes rochas no Parque Estadual Cânion do Rio Poti.
articles.body:
Rochas gigantes no Piauí guardam desenhos misteriosos de animais, figuras humanas e outros símbolos — Foto: Ascom Semarh

Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Gravuras rupestres de animais, figuras humanas e símbolos ainda desconhecidos estão ameaçadas por pichações, avanço de plantações e criação de animais nas proximidades de um sítio arqueológico identificado no Parque Estadual Cânion do Rio Poti , no Norte do Piauí.

O local fica na comunidade Conceição dos Marreiros, em Buriti dos Montes , e ocupa aproximadamente 1 hectare. A área reúne desenhos espalhados por grandes blocos de rocha, entre eles representações de lagartos, figuras semelhantes a crianças e imagens do sol.

Segundo a Secretaria de Estado do Meio Ambiente e Recursos Hídricos (Semarh), os registros foram feitos por meio da técnica de picoteamento, que consiste em produzir pequenas marcas na superfície das rochas para formar figuras.

Apesar de o sítio estar dentro dos limites do parque estadual, a preservação das gravuras enfrenta desafios. Entre os problemas identificados estão pichações nas rochas e o avanço de atividades como plantações e criação de animais nas proximidades .

Diante desse cenário, o governo estuda a possibilidade de criar uma unidade de conservação municipal para ampliar a proteção da área e do patrimônio arqueológico.

Segundo o secretário de Estado do Meio Ambiente, Feliphe Araújo, a iniciativa busca reforçar a preservação de áreas com riqueza natural e histórica ainda pouco conhecidas.

"Estamos trabalhando para ampliar a proteção dos nossos patrimônios naturais e históricos. Essas gravuras mostram a riqueza arqueológica do Parque Estadual Cânion do Rio Poti e reforçam a importância de preservar áreas que ainda são pouco conhecidas", afirmou.

articles.title: Feds have added mitigation strategies, local aid ahead of lead azide detonation
articles.summary: What started as a plan to detonate nearly 5 tons of degraded explosive material in Iowa, with coordination between the U.S. Army and the U.S. Environmental P...
articles.body:
What started as a plan to detonate nearly 5 tons of degraded explosive material in Iowa, with coordination between the U.S. Army and the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, has since triggered multiple state emergency responses and an "unprecedented" coordination of federal agencies.

The detonation is scheduled for Wednesday about 9 a.m. at the U.S. Army's ammunition plant in Middletown in southeast Iowa. The scheduled time follows numerous delays over the past week from the Army, a lawsuit, intervention from the president, and widespread public concern of the health and environmental effects associated with detonating a lead-based explosive.

Lead deposition maps released by the Army Tuesday morning show lead released by the detonation could be dispersed in the air as far as 100 miles southwest of Middletown and cross into Missouri. An additional map shows there is a potential for lead surface dust to settle as far as 50 miles southwest of the detonation site.

The Army has recommended, and FEMA is supporting, the evacuation of Iowans in Middletown and the immediate area – a 5-mile cone to the southwest of the detonation site – during the detonation period.

Soldiers, environmental teams and other federal officials are in the area helping to sample soils and alert residents of the detonation plans. The Army will be releasing maps, adjusted for the latest weather conditions, six hours ahead of detonation and every hour leading up to detonation.

A slew of federal officials from the Army, the EPA, Department of Health and Human Services, Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, and Firearms, Department of Agriculture and more gathered at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant Tuesday for a press conference and shared new information with the public about the response.

When the detonation was originally announced , the Army recommended individuals in a select neighborhood of Middletown evacuate during the detonation, due to concerns that the blast could cause some windows to shatter.

After nearly a week of nationwide, public outcry and calls from politicians for greater protections of the surrounding area, additional efforts are in place to mitigate the amount of lead dust that is emitted, and the government is working to help Iowans in the area.

Speaking at the press conference Tuesday, Sean Kaufman with HHS said the highest risk is for pregnant individuals, children, or people with chronic illnesses who live or plan to be in the areas the Army forecasts will be impacted.

FEMA has a hotline available, 1-800-621-3362, and has sent out emergency alerts to cellphones in the area about the planned detonation. Additional assistance can be found online .

"You definitely want to be out of that area," Kaufman said of the at-risk groups. "I would evacuate that area that's signaled in the model."

A press release from the Lee County Sheriff's Office said Tuesday that U.S. Army soldiers would begin going door to door to "notify residents" of recommended evacuations.

FEMA Administrator Cameron Hamilton said at the news conference that the White House has made it "very very clear that we are to spare no expense to ensure that Americans are kept safe."

Hamilton said it has been "made clear" to communities southwest of the detonation site that "if they choose to relocate, we will offer services." He said FEMA is offering transportation, food and relocation assistance to those in the impacted areas. The Army release said short-term lodging will be provided to eligible Iowans through Friday, Nov. 27.

Hamilton noted that the maps shared by the Army represent "some of the worst case scenarios" of the lead dispersion.

"We care deeply about the American people," Hamilton said. "What you see here is not red, not blue, it's red, white, and blue. This is the very best of the American's team."

Gov. Kim Reynolds issued a disaster proclamation Tuesday for Des Moines, Lee and Van Buren counties for the planned detonation, activating the response plans for the counties and state agencies.

According to a news release from the governor, the Iowa Department of Health and Human Services is working with federal partners, as well as other state agencies, and evaluating potential public impacts. The department is also providing precautionary guidance to communities and informing local public health partners.

The Iowa Department of Natural Resources is assessing Army, EPA and other federal plans for pre- and post-detonation monitoring of air, land and water quality and the Iowa Department of Agriculture and Land Stewardship has published new guidance for livestock producers within 20 miles of Middletown based on most recent weather information.

As many as 100 Iowa National Guard soldiers will be available to aid local, state and federal agencies in their public safety plans, the release stated. They will also help provide guidance and assistance to around 150 households with a temporary evacuation.

"Today's briefing by the U.S. Army highlighted the responsible planning and coordination that have gone into the upcoming detonation. I greatly appreciate their due diligence, responsible approach, and focus on the public health and safety of Iowans in nearby communities," Reynolds said in the release. "Iowa agencies are actively engaged alongside our federal and local partners, and we remain focused on ensuring communities have the information and resources they need before, during, and after the operation."

Missouri Gov. Mike Kehoe has also launched a state emergency center and Illinois Governor J.B Pritzker said he has put state agencies on alert, though the plume models don't currently show the state will be impacted.

"While risk to Missourians remains minimal, our State Emergency Operations Center is activated and our state agencies continue to be in constant contact with federal partners to take the necessary actions to protect the health and safety of our citizens, livestock, and environment," Kehoe said in a statement.

Feds have 'continuously added' mitigation protocol

Politicians, Iowans and environmental groups have repeatedly called for more transparency from the Army and associated federal partners since the original plans for the detonation were released.

Sen.-elect Josh Turek of Iowa called the Tuesday news conference "long-overdue."

"I've repeatedly reiterated that Iowans' health and safety must be the number one priority in the execution of this operation, and that transparency and clear communication – both of which have been sorely lacking up to this point – are paramount," Turek said in a statement Tuesday.

At the news conference, acting Secretary of the Army Hon. Adam Telle emphasized that the government's priority was the "health and safety of the citizens of this region."

Telle said those involved have sought advice from "every expert" in and outside of the federal government and have considered all viable options and data before reaching the conclusion to proceed with detonation.

"There is consensus across the experts across the country that a controlled, mitigated detonation of the lead azide here at Iowa Army Ammunition Plant, is far preferable to an uncontrolled spontaneous detonation of that substance," Telle said.

Some of those mitigations include: sand around the structure holding the barrels; two walls of four, 16,000-gallon water tanks; a plan to "flood" the exterior of the storage area with aqueous foam to help absorb particulate matter from the blast; and modeling to forecast impacted areas based on weather conditions.

The "water walls," as Telle called them, and the foam were not part of the Army's originally released detonation plans.

Telle said federal agencies have been working "24 hours a day" the past several days on the situation in Middletown and have "continuously added" mitigation measures.

"There has been unprecedented collaboration across the federal government," Telle said. "Unprecedented."

He also emphasized that "every reliable bit of information" the government has over the next 24 hours is "going to be made available to the public."

Maj. Gen. Eric Shirley, commander of the Army Sustainment Command, said there has been "multi-agency" work on the situation since the degraded lead azide was discovered in March.

"This is not simply an Army problem set, nor will it be an Army solution. It is a whole of government response," Shirley said.

U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives director Rob Cekada said lead azide is a "sensitive" primary explosive that has been phased out by the government for around 15 years.

Cekada said in 2009 the "nation's stockpile" of lead azide — nearly 10,000 pounds of the material, some of which he said was "already 60 plus years old" — was moved to the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant.

Information filed by the government in a legal case about the issue said that the barrels were visually checked monthly and annually refilled with a solution of water and ethanol. The crystallization that the Army noticed in March meant that this year the mixture couldn't be administered, for fear of setting the explosives off. Cekada said this means there is less liquid in the barrels, making them more susceptible to the approaching freezing temperatures.

Cekada said the stockpile was intended to be kept at IAAAP in the event that the U.S. military needed to deploy lead azide as a primary explosive again.

Col. Aaron Teller, the Army Explosive Ordnance Disposal commander executing the detonation, said the last major disposal of lead azide was in 1977 in Colorado. He said that detonation had "zero mitigation" in place and only 25% of lead material from that detonation was released into the atmosphere.

"So we believe we can significantly reduce that last 25% with the mitigation strategy that we have in place," Teller said.

Thomas Croci, with the EPA's Office of National Security and Operations Coordination, said the agency had a "blanket" of sampling teams out in the region collecting before-detonation samples and preparing to collect samples following the detonation.

EPA sampling requests should be directed to 1-833-649-9624. More information can be found on the EPA response site .

"No one should feel like they will not get a sample," Croci said. "If you want your home sampled, your property sampled, your school sampled, you will get that sample and the EPA will assist with that sampling."

Croci said there are "more than 150 teams" sampling areas in three states, and have four mobile laboratories deployed to test air toxins and "anything that comes off the combustion."

Richard Fordyce, an under secretary at USDA, said the department estimates 350 farms in Iowa and Missouri will be potentially impacted by the detonation.

The USDA posted on X that it was working with Iowa and Missouri officials to "protect livestock, support producers and safeguard our food supply." The department recommended farmers shelter or move their livestock from the region and contact veterinarians if they suspect animals were exposed to lead.

Iowa Secretary of Agriculture Mike Naig told reporters Tuesday in Ames that it's "unfortunate" that the situation in Middletown has reached the point where detonation is the only option, and he thinks questions will need to be answered after the detonation as to how things got to this point and where communication broke down.

"I think that obviously the late notice to the state has caused a lot of work now over a short number of days, so I think that could have been handled differently," Naig said. "But here we are, and we need to get through this, and we need to make sure that Iowans have their questions answered, and that our farmers, at least in my lane here, we want to make sure that our farmers are supported through the process."

With harvests essentially complete for the year, Naig said the Iowa Department of Agriculture is focusing on helping livestock producers prepare for the detonation and record what they can before and after for testing and compensation if necessary.

"There's a lot of things that'll have to be determined after we see the impact and what kind of levels we see. And there's all kinds of monitoring that'll be going on in the area," Naig said.

This story has been updated with newer maps from the Army.

articles.title: 6 killed when plane crashes off Mississippi
articles.summary: Six people were killed Tuesday when the plane they were traveling in crashed off the coast of Mississippi, authorities said.
articles.body: Six people were killed Tuesday when the plane they were traveling in crashed off the coast of Mississippi, authorities said. The bodies of all six people, including two children, who were on board the Cessna 210 have been recovered, the U.S. Coast Guard said, late Tuesday after an hours-long search. “This is a heartbreaking outcome, and our deepest sympathies are with the families and loved ones who are facing an unimaginable loss,” said Cmdr. Trevor Blount, a Coast Guard search and rescue coordinator. Divers from the Mississippi Department of Marine Resources found the victims in the plane’s fuselage, the Coast Guard’s Heartland District office in New Orleans said in a statement Tuesday night. The single-engine, high-wing aircraft went down 2 miles northeast of Horn Island, Mississippi, the Coast Guard said. Coast Guard teams in the water and air were joined by crews from the Air Force, FBI and area county and city first responders, it said, searching those waters for roughly four hours before the state divers made the discovery. Juan Ros, a public affairs officer for the Coast Guard Mobile Sector, said earlier interview that those on board included two boys ages 8 and 10. The Cessna 210 plane went down around 3:30 p.m. near Pascagoula, Mississippi, according to the FAA. “That’s when they lost communication,” Ros said, adding that radar showed the plane descending “at 10,000 feet per minute.” The plane was traveling from New Orleans to Fort Myers, Florida. Crews searched two nautical miles northeast of Horn Island, a barrier island on the Gulf Coast that is designated as a wilderness area and only accessible by private boat. The NTSB will lead the investigation, according to the FAA.

articles.title: US court convicts China’s Huawei for fraud, conspiring to steal trade secrets, in sprawling trial over Iran business
articles.summary: Chinese telecommunications equipment maker Huawei was convicted by a jury in New York City on Tuesday in a sprawling US criminal case on charges that it deceived banks about its business in Iran and stole trade secrets from American companies.
articles.body: Chinese telecommunications equipment maker Huawei was convicted by a jury in New York City on Tuesday in a sprawling US criminal case on charges that it deceived banks about its business in Iran and stole trade secrets from American companies. The verdict came in a criminal case that began in 2018, with the US government the following year placing Huawei on a trade blacklist that restricted its access to US technology amid American concerns that Huawei posed national security risks. The jury in Brooklyn federal court found Huawei guilty on 10 of the 12 criminal counts the company faced, including bank fraud, wire fraud, sanctions violations and conspiring to steal trade secrets. The jury acquitted Huawei of conspiring to obstruct justice and racketeering conspiracy, a charge alleging the company had acted as a criminal enterprise. The trial lasted more than two months, with prosecutors calling more than 60 witnesses and the defense calling 15. It was not immediately clear what penalties Huawei will face when US District Judge Ann Donnelly sentences it on September 14, 2027. Reuters stories in 2012 and 2013 helped expose Huawei’s activities in Iran and were discussed during the trial. “After the media started questioning Huawei’s operations in Iran, so did Huawei’s banks,” prosecutor Meredith Arfa told jurors during closing arguments in the case last week. Brian Heberlig, a lawyer for Huawei, said the company was disappointed by the convictions but said the acquittal on the racketeering conspiracy charge vindicated its “good-faith compliance culture.” “We fully expect to appeal,” Heberlig told reporters. US Attorney Joseph Nocella said in a statement: “Few crimes are as serious as Huawei’s decades-long pattern of endangering US national security, violating the sanctity of US commerce, and impeding the enforcement of US laws.” China’s embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Asked how much the company may have to pay in penalties, Heberlig said it was premature to comment, but said the acquittal on the racketeering conspiracy charge could make a significant difference. Experts have said the case did not undermine Huawei’s business, as the company diversified and emerged as a key player in China’s push for artificial intelligence. Founder’s daughter was detained In December 2018, Meng Wanzhou, Huawei’s chief financial officer and daughter of the company’s founder, was detained in Canada on a US warrant, prompting a diplomatic crisis involving the United States, China and Canada. Meng had been secretly indicted on US charges of misleading an HSBC banker about Huawei’s business in Iran, so the company could move dollars in and out of Iran in violation of American sanctions. Meng fought extradition to the US for nearly three years, before entering a deferred prosecution agreement and flying home to China to a hero’s welcome. The charges against her were dropped. Meng did not testify at trial, though an HSBC banker she met with in 2013 did testify. The 2018 indictment alleged that Huawei misled HSBC, Standard Chartered and BNP Paribas about its business dealings in Iran. Prosecutors added new charges in 2020, including allegations that Huawei conspired to steal trade secrets from US technology companies over two decades. The prosecution case During the trial, prosecutors sought to prove that Huawei stole source code from Cisco Systems for its routers, stole wireless telecommunications company Quintel’s antenna technology, and hired a professor to gain access to a circuit board developed by semiconductor company CNEX. Jurors watched a video that, according to prosecutors, showed a Huawei employee slipping a piece of a T-Mobile testing robot into his backpack, and heard about a Huawei engineer sneaking into a Fujitsu booth at a trade show to photograph a device. Prosecutors gave jurors a statement attached to Meng’s deferred prosecution agreement in which she acknowledged that the company illegally conducted business in Iran. The defense argued that HSBC and the other banks knew about Huawei’s business in Iran and were competing for Huawei’s business. Heberlig accused prosecutors during his closing argument of having “cherry-picked” a handful of disparate incidents to support their claim of a 20-year conspiracy. Heberlig said Huawei succeeded through “hard work, innovation, and investment in research and development.” The company has more than 200,000 employees and operates in approximately 170 countries.

articles.title: Cambridge students uncover a 1,100-year-old pit holding 10 bodies, including a 6-foot-5-inch man with a surgically drilled hole in his skull; archaeologists investigate a possible Viking-era execution
articles.summary: A possible Viking-era execution pit uncovered by Cambridge archaeology students at Wandlebury Country Park, on the outskirts of the city, has revealed the
articles.body: A possible Viking-era execution pit uncovered by Cambridge archaeology students at Wandlebury Country Park, on the outskirts of the city, has revealed the remains of ten people from around the ninth century. Some skeletons are complete while other bodies were dismembered, and one young man stood far taller than his contemporaries. The burial lies in a former borderland where Saxon and Viking kingdoms fought repeatedly for territory, and researchers are weighing whether it records a battle, a mass punishment or a mixture of both. Nothing was buried alongside the dead to identify them, so their origins and allegiances remain unresolved.A student training dig at Wandlebury Country Park turned up the site's most grisly find to dateAccording to the University of Cambridge and its Department of Archaeology, the burial pit came to light in spring and summer 2025 during a teaching excavation for undergraduate archaeology students. The dig was led by Oscar Aldred of the Cambridge Archaeological Unit at Wandlebury, three miles south of Cambridge. The park is known for the banks and ditches of an Iron Age hillfort built a thousand years before the Viking era. Measuring four metres by one, the pit lay just outside that ringwork to the south.The park's owner, the charity Cambridge Past, Present and Future, has hosted student digs there for several years, though never one this significant. Olivia Courtney, an archaeology student from Bath, told the University of Cambridge that before the first remains appeared, "our best find was a 1960s Smarties lid". These were the first human remains found at the park since 1976, when a storm uprooted a tree nearby and exposed five skeletons from the same period. The discovery also featured in an episode of the BBC series Digging for Britain.Complete skeletons, a stack of legs and loose skulls made the burial unusual even for a mass graveFour men lay in the pit as complete skeletons, some positioned as though they had been tied up. Around and above them were skulls with no obvious matching bodies, a stack of legs, and other remains from ribs to pelvises, with parts of the same kind sometimes grouped. All appear to have been relatively young men, discarded without care.Mixing intact and dismembered remains is highly unusual even for a mass grave, and it has puzzled the archaeologists involved. One man was clearly beheaded, shown by chop marks on his jaw, and a few others carry traces of injury consistent with combat. Those injuries are too few, however, to prove that the group died in battle.An extremely tall young man with a healed hole in his skull may have lived with a growth conditionThe most striking individual was a man aged between 17 and 24, thrown face down into the pit. He would have stood about six feet five inches tall, towering over the average male height of around five feet six inches at the time. A large oval hole, three centimetres across, on the back left of his skull suggests trepanation, an ancient operation in which a hole is bored through a living person's skull. The edges show signs of healing.Trepanned skulls have been found around the world, including from ancient Greece and Rome, where the procedure was thought to ease migraines, seizures and conditions now understood as psychological.Trish Biers, curator of the Duckworth Collection at the University of Cambridge, to which the remains were taken for analysis, told the university that his height may stem from a tumour affecting the pituitary gland, which released excess growth hormones. She said this shows in the long shafts of his limb bones. Biers added that such a tumour would have raised pressure inside the skull and caused headaches, which the surgery may have been an attempt to relieve.Archaeologists doubt a battle alone explains the bodies and consider punishment at a meeting placeOscar Aldred told the university that the way the remains were handled points to terrible violence and possibly an execution. He suggested those buried may have received corporal punishment connected to Wandlebury's standing as a sacred or well-known gathering point. Some of the detached body parts, he said, may earlier have been displayed as trophies, then collected and buried with the executed or otherwise slaughtered men.Aldred also noted there is little evidence of deliberate chopping up of those parts. They may instead have been decomposing and falling apart by the time they went into the pit.Radiocarbon dating points to Saxon and Viking wars, but whether the dead were Vikings is unprovenIn the late eighth century, Cambridge belonged to Offa, ruler of the Saxon kingdom of Mercia. Around 874 to 875, half of the Viking Great Army camped near the town and sacked it. Cambridgeshire was then absorbed into the Viking kingdom of East Anglia and stayed under Viking control into the early tenth century under the Danelaw agreement. Aldred described the county as a frontier region between Mercia and East Anglia, scarred by decades of Saxon and Viking warfare, and said the pit may relate to those conflicts.Initial radiocarbon work dates the tall man's skeleton to between the years 772 and 891, with 85 per cent probability, and places other bones around the time of the Viking sacking. Further dating work is planned to narrow that window.Genetic analysis, chemical testing of bones and a new survey aim to reveal who lay in the pitHistoric England, which supports the excavation and oversees archaeology on protected sites such as Wandlebury, commissioned a fresh geophysical survey of the surrounding area. Tony Calladine, the organisation's East of England regional director, told the university that the discovery speaks to the story of the nation and the lives of ordinary people in turbulent times.The Cambridge team set out plans for bone analysis, including ancient genetic material and chemical signatures in the bones, to investigate health, kinship and ancestry. It also intends to attempt refitting, matching dismembered pieces together to work out how many people were thrown into the pit.For the students, the find was sobering. Grace Grandfield, an undergraduate from York who took part, told the Department of Archaeology that it was "a shocking contrast to the peaceful site of Wandlebury". Several of the people uncovered were close to her own age.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Israel’s Eisenkot secures first coalition partner in bid to form government
articles.summary: The Yashar party says it agreed to sign a coalition pact with Israel’s Our Home party, led by Avigdor Lieberman.
articles.body:
Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party has announced an agreement to unite with a right-wing opposition party in a bid to form the next Israeli government following October’s elections .

The Yashar party said on Tuesday that it agreed to sign a coalition pact with Israel’s Our Home party after a meeting with its leader Avigdor Lieberman, the first alliance of its kind since the election.

After no party managed to secure a 61-seat majority, Israel’s parliament was sworn in on November 10 without a new government.

President Isaac Herzog tasked Eisenkot with forming ⁠a government, while Benjamin Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister despite the October 27 election stripping Netanyahu of his majority.

Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government under a 28-day mandate, though he could ask for a 14-day extension. If Eisenkot fails, Netanyahu would have an opportunity to do so. If no one is able to form a government, another election will be held next year.

The agreement between Eisenkot, whose party won 21 parliament seats, and Lieberman, whose party won seven, was unforeseen since Lieberman has been vocal about his opposition to forming a government with support from Arab parties as well as to a unity government with Netanyahu.

Lieberman had once served as foreign minister under a previous Netanyahu government but has since become a strong critic.

Netanyahu’s right-wing Likud’s alliance with far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties outperformed election expectations but still lost its majority. It now holds 53 of the Knesset’s 120 seats.

Eisenkot’s centre-right Yashar party and patchwork coalition partners, including Lieberman, hold just 48 seats. But they have potential allies in the parties representing Israel’s Arab minority, which hold 19 seats and ⁠are aligned with Eisenkot in their vehement opposition to Netanyahu.

Talks are also ongoing between Eisenkot, some of his “change bloc” partners and Likud on forming a unity government.

The left-wing Democrats party, which won eight parliament seats, separately said it was suspending talks with Eisenkot after the Yashar party leader’s talks with Netanyahu’s Likud on a possible unity government.

Yair Golan, head of the Democrats, said he prefers a government without Netanyahu but with Arab parties.

articles.title: Beau Lamarre: Sydney police officer convicted of murder of Jesse Baird and Luke Davies
articles.summary: Beau Lamarre was on Wednesday found guilty of murdering his ex Jesse Baird, and Baird's new partner Luke Davies.
articles.body:
It was just after 09:00 on a warm February morning when CCTV picked up a man dressed as an UberEats rider hovering on a sidewalk in one of Sydney's wealthiest neighbourhoods.

He dawdled for around 20 minutes, "steeling himself for what he was about to do" prosecutors say, before disappearing out of sight. Minutes later another CCTV camera captured the sound of gunshots ringing out.

Former police officer Beau Lamarre, 31, was on Wednesday found guilty of murdering his former partner Jesse Baird, a TV presenter, and Luke Davies, Baird's new partner, with his work-issued gun.

In February 2024, the bloodied belongings of Baird and Davies were found in a skip in the suburb of Cronulla, sparking a frantic search for the couple. It culminated in the discovery of their bodies on a rural property, partially buried beneath sticks and debris.

During a two-month trial filled with at-times extraordinary testimony and a wealth of CCTV evidence, the court heard Lamarre had planned his crime over months.

Jurors watched CCTV of the then police officer purchasing a surfboard bag in which to put Baird's body, after casually sizing it up against a friend in the shop, and heard from a stream of former friends and colleagues who testified that Lamarre asked them for advice about everything from mobile phone signals to where he could buy a gun.

One recounted the chilling moment Lamarre told her that if he were ever to murder someone, he would leave their belongings in a dumpster and hide the body in bushland where they would never be found.

"What would you do if I told you I killed somebody? Would you help me hide the body?" he asked, according to her testimony.

Later, Lamarre asked for help in covering up the killings; his friends - none of whom have been implicated - say they began receiving panicked calls and odd requests from him.

One told the court Lamarre persuaded her to go for a drive in the country, during which he tried to dispose of the bodies at the family farm of a man he'd met on a dating app. Over the speakers, he played Taylor Swift's No Body, No Crime.

Baird, 26, and Lamarre - a one-time celebrity blogger who also had his own swimwear line on the side of his police work - met in a nightclub in October 2022. For Lamarre, it quickly became an infatuation, but for Baird, an AFL referee and former Network Ten presenter, the relationship appeared to be casual.

After discovering in April 2023 that Lamarre had gone through messages on his phone, and unfollowed other men on his Instagram account, Baird broke it off.

But Lamarre's obsession only grew. He watched Baird having sex with another man through his bedroom window, broke into his house multiple times, deleting contacts on his phone and turning on location settings so that he could engineer meetings with the TV presenter.

On one occasion Baird woke up to find Lamarre in his bedroom; not realising who it was, he chased him down the street. Lamarre was also convicted of aggravated break and enter over that incident on Wednesday.

Prosecutor Brett Hatfield said Baird was "oblivious to the accused's scheming and manipulations", and the pair briefly rekindled the relationship before Baird ended it definitively in November.

He'd discovered Lamarre had, again, been accessing his phone and had attempted to ward off a love rival by pretending to have received flowers from Baird.

His pride wounded, Hatfield said Lamarre's thoughts turned to a "darker place": "revenge".

He asked an old friend if her ex-partner could get him a gun: "This was the beginning of the plan for the murder," the prosecutor said.

In the months leading up to the killings, Lamarre bought a burner phone, a motorcycle helmet, and practised shooting in the woods. On holiday with a friend in Bali in January 2024 he tried to buy a silencer.

While his murder plans percolated, he also began lashing out with petty acts of malice, prosecutors said, such as putting water in the fuel tank of Baird's car.

But at the same time as he plotted, Lamarre was still trying to win his ex back.

On one occasion he pressured a friend to send Baird a 1,600-word message he had himself composed, claiming that he had cancer, and may need to have his arm amputated.

Under questioning in court, he said a naturopath he couldn't remember the name of had diagnosed him with "a form of sporadic cancer".

By the end of 2023, Baird had met and hit it off with Davies, 29. "It was early days but they were both smitten with each other," his mother, Helen Baird, told the court. He sent her a picture of the pair at a Pink concert. "I just sent a big love heart and said 'I'm so happy for both of you'."

Early on the morning of 19 February, Lamarre picked up a hire car he had asked his mother to rent and drove to Baird's home. After waiting several hours for Baird's housemates to leave, while disguised as an UberEats driver, he let himself in with a key he had copied.

Lamarre told the court he had been at Baird's home to pick up some belongings , including a A$25,000 (US$16,500, £12,600) Cartier ring, and had disguised himself to avoid the embarrassment of being recognised if anyone was home.

He claimed he let himself in when no one answered the door, and the two men were killed in separate struggles. He argued that Baird had been holding a knife and the first shot was fired to disarm him, and the second by accident. Davies shot himself when he grabbed the gun, Lamarre said.

But prosecutors told the jury Baird was shot in the back and then once again through his temple as he lay gravely wounded on the kitchen floor.

The evidence, Hatfield said, pointed to one thing only: "an execution".

Davies was then shot through a bedroom door as he tried to call emergency services. The court heard the panic in his voice as the seconds-long call was replayed before it dropped out.

After that, Lamarre set about trying to hide the evidence of what Hatfield called his "brazen and shocking murders".

One of his first actions was to call a friend. He testified Lamarre confessed he had "killed people" and asked him to take a day off work "to help him clean up his mess".

Later Lamarre pretended the call was a joke, saying, "Did you like my Oscar performance? Got you".

Meanwhile, Lamarre went to a DIY store to purchase mops, bleach and bin bags. After returning to Baird's house to clean up, he left the bodies wrapped in surfboard bags and tarpaulins in the courtyard.

Baird had been set to move out that week, and Lamarre used Baird's phone to reassure his housemates he had hired an Airtasker to move his belongings, adding, "I might be flying to Perth tonight".

Baird's housemates quickly spotted the surfboard bags when they returned home, snapping a photograph tendered in court which showed "red liquid" seeping out.

"I thought it was rusted water from the outdoor furniture," one of the women said.

The surfboard bags were gone the next morning.

Lamarre had hired a van, and over the next two days made more trips to the DIY store and a sports shop to buy gumboots, a wheelbarrow, bigger surfboard bags and 10kg weights. He squeezed in a hospital appointment for a minor procedure and paused for a sushi date with a friend, CCTV showing him laughing and eating as the bodies lay in the back of his van.

On 21 February, he picked up another friend in the van for what she thought was lunch.

There were blue tarps in the back and it smelled "lemony", she told the court. She "wasn't allowed to put the windows up or turn the aircon off" as they motored towards Goulburn, 200km southwest of Sydney, stopping only at another DIY store, where he asked her to buy an angle grinder.

His friend told the court she remembers Lamarre playing No Body, No Crime at some point: "It's a very niche song."

Arriving at a farm owned by a Hinge date's family, Lamarre used the angle grinder to cut through a padlock, making his way to a dam where he unsuccessfully tried to sink the bodies.

It was now late at night and he drove his friend, by this time upset and confused, home before returning to retrieve the bodies. He then left them in the van, parked in Sydney overnight, before driving once more to Goulburn, where he dumped the bodies near a monastery.

Later that day he visited another friend, telling her to look up the definition of schizophrenia and asking whether he could use her hose, because "there was a bit of blood he had to scrub off" the hired van, the court heard.

By this time police were closing in, and on 23 February Lamarre went to turn himself in at Bondi police station. On the way, he called a police helpline.

"I've been bullied by multiple New South Wales police force members," he told the woman on the other end of the line. "All this stress and trauma and psychological abuse and trauma - did I say trauma already? - has caused me to not sleep, get anxious, it's caused me to have some symptoms of schizophrenia."

"Actually sorry, you know what, can you just... delete that whole thing. We'll just keep it short and sweet."

He wasn't sure when he'd be back to work, he said. Shortly afterwards he was arrested and charged with murder , and the bodies of Baird and Davies were found four days later.

Lamarre's lawyer John Stratton insisted he'd acted in self-defence and had "panicked" realising how the scene would look to outsiders.

The former police officer did plenty of "foolish" and "unusual" things - "He was, it's fair to say, a poorly behaved boyfriend," Stratton said - but that did not make him a murderer.

Ultimately, however, the jury was not convinced and took just over an hour to convict him. He will be sentenced in March and faces life in prison.
